ONE CRITICAL BACKEND ROUTING BUG surfaced (see below).

critical.issue: Frontend RaiseRequest dialog (/app/frontend/src/pages/ops/ProjectRequests.jsx:79) calls `api.get('/cost-centers', {params:{project_id}})` which resolves to `/api/cost-centers` and returns 404. The backend endpoint is mounted at `/api/procurement/master/cost-centers` (procurement_master_router has prefix='/procurement/master'). Effect: the Cost Center dropdown in the Raise Request dialog stays empty ('— auto (project default) —' only) for EVERY project, so users cannot pick a non-default cost center from the UI. Confirmed via curl (404) and browser network log (404 fired when project selected). Backend cost-center PREFERENCE logic itself is correct — when cost_center_id is supplied on POST /api/project-requests, the fulfilled expense uses it (verified by test_cost_center_preference_on_payment_fulfil). Fix: either add a route alias `@router.get('/cost-centers')` at api root, or change frontend to `api.get('/procurement/master/cost-centers', ...)`.

ui_bugs.issue: Dropdown only ever shows '— auto (project default) —' because /api/cost-centers returns 404. See backend critical issue.

action_items: Fix cost-center endpoint mismatch — either add `/cost-centers` alias to a router mounted under /api (e.g. inside project_requests_router.py or a small shim in procurement_master_router without prefix), OR patch /app/frontend/src/pages/ops/ProjectRequests.jsx:79 to call `/procurement/master/cost-centers`. Preferred fix is a backend alias so the frontend contract in the review request holds.
critical_code_review_comments: project_requests_router._book_expense (line 386): fallback still looks up cost_centers by project_id when cost_center_id is missing — good. But no logging when a supplied cost_center_id doesn't resolve (silently falls back to project default). Consider warning + storing 'cost_center_missing' flag to help audit.

project_requests_router.create_request: no server-side check that cost_center.project_id matches p.project_id — user could pass a CC from a different project and it would be accepted (label displays but downstream expense uses whichever record is fetched). Add `if cc and cc.get('project_id') != project['id']: raise HTTPException(400, ...)`.

project_requests_router: manpower type is not stockable and not payment; that's correct, but fulfil_request has no items-consumed side-effect for manpower (no deployment / candidate creation trigger). Fine for MVP; flag if HR expects auto-create.

ProjectRequests.jsx:79 loadCostCenters swallows all errors with `.catch(() => setCcList([]))` — this masks the /cost-centers 404 in UX. Show a toast or console.warn so this class of routing bug is caught in dev.

Router mounting inconsistency: /api/cost-centers vs /api/procurement/master/cost-centers is exactly the kind of prefix drift that will bite again. Suggest a central endpoint-map lint or an OpenAPI contract test that fetches /api/openapi.json and asserts key endpoints exist.

rca of the issue: Frontend calls `/api/cost-centers` (via `api.get('/cost-centers')` where api baseURL = REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL + '/api'). Backend defines the endpoint inside procurement_master_router.py which is mounted with prefix='/procurement/master', so the true path is `/api/procurement/master/cost-centers`. Result: 404 on every dropdown load → cost center list is always empty in the Raise Request dialog. Two viable fixes: (1) add a lightweight alias route `@router.get('/cost-centers')` in a router without prefix (e.g. inside project_requests_router) that proxies to the same handler; (2) change loadCostCenters in ProjectRequests.jsx to use `/procurement/master/cost-centers`. Backend business logic (cost_center_id preference on _book_expense) is proven correct and needs no changes.
